candidates.workingClaim: January 16, 2006: On January 16, 2006, Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, the first woman elected head of state of an African country, was sworn in as president of Liberia.
January 16, 1992: On January 16, 1992, the civil war in El Salvador ended as the government and the Farabundo Marti National Liberation Front signed the Chapultepec Peace Accords in Mexico City.
January 16, 1978: On January 16, 1978, NASA announced its newest class of astronauts, which for the first time included six women.
January 16, 1556: On January 16, 1556, Charles V, Holy Roman emperor and king of Spain, renounced his claim to Spain.
January 16, 1883: On January 16, 1883, the Pendleton Civil Service Act established the Civil Service Commission in the United States.
January 17, 1929: On January 17, 1929, Popeye, the sailor known for his love of spinach, made his debut in the comic strip Thimble Theatre.
January 17, 1706: On January 17, 1706, Benjamin Franklin was born. He later helped draft the US Declaration of Independence.
January 17, 1893: On January 17, 1893, Hawaii's Queen Liliuokalani was deposed by a provisional government led by Sanford Ballard Dole.
January 17, 1961: On January 17, 1961, in his farewell address, US President Dwight D. Eisenhower warned against the acquisition of unwarranted influence by the military-industrial complex.
January 17, 1995: On January 17, 1995, a large-scale earthquake struck the Osaka-Kobe (Hanshin) metropolitan area of Japan, killing about 6,400 people.
January 18, 1871: On January 18, 1871, the German Empire was founded under the leadership of Otto von Bismarck.
January 18, 1911: On January 18, 1911, the American pilot Eugene Ely performed the first aircraft landing on a ship's flight deck.
January 18, 2002: On January 18, 2002, the civil war in Sierra Leone was officially declared over. More than 50,000 people are estimated to have died.
January 18, 1958: On January 18, 1958, Willie O'Ree became the first Black athlete to play in a National Hockey League game.
January 18, 1882: On January 18, 1882, A.A. Milne, the author who created Winnie-the-Pooh, was born in London.
January 19, 1853: On January 19, 1853, Giuseppe Verdi's opera Il trovatore premiered in Rome.
January 19, 1809: On January 19, 1809, the writer Edgar Allan Poe was born in Boston.
January 19, 1825: On January 19, 1825, Ezra Daggett and Thomas Kensett obtained a patent for a preservation process used to store food in tin cans.
January 19, 1955: On January 19, 1955, US President Dwight D. Eisenhower held the first-ever televised presidential press conference.
January 20, 2009: On January 20, 2009, Barack Obama was sworn in as the 44th president of the United States, the first African American to hold the office.
January 20, 1981: On January 20, 1981, the Iran hostage crisis ended when 52 Americans who had been held hostage for 15 months were released.
January 20, 1778: On January 20, 1778, the British explorer James Cook landed at Waimea, on the island of Kauai in Hawaii.
January 20, 1973: On January 20, 1973, Amilcar Lopes Cabral was assassinated while leading the effort to secure Guinea-Bissau's independence.
January 20, 1920: On January 20, 1920, the Italian director Federico Fellini, one of the most celebrated filmmakers of the post-World War II period, was born.
January 21, 1976: On January 21, 1976, Concorde, a supersonic commercial aircraft built with funding from the British and French governments, began regular service.
January 21, 1793: On January 21, 1793, during the French Revolution, Louis XVI, the last Bourbon king of France before the Revolution, was executed by guillotine in Paris.
January 21, 1924: On January 21, 1924, Vladimir Lenin, the founder of the Soviet state, died.
January 21, 1905: On January 21, 1905, the fashion designer Christian Dior was born in Granville, France.
January 21, 1941: On January 21, 1941, the singer Placido Domingo was born in Madrid.
January 22, 1901: On January 22, 1901, Queen Victoria died at age 81 after reigning for more than 60 years.
January 22, 1905: On January 22, 1905, Russian workers marching in St. Petersburg were fired on by Russian troops. The day became known as Bloody Sunday.
January 22, 2006: On January 22, 2006, Evo Morales was sworn in as president of Bolivia, the first person of Indigenous descent to hold that office.
January 22, 1992: On January 22, 1992, Roberta Bondar became the first Canadian woman and the first neurologist to travel into space.
January 22, 1788: On January 22, 1788, Lord Byron, the British Romantic poet and satirist who captured the imagination of Europe, was born.
